masthead.headline: Nine days, six steps, and one of them cost four times its estimate.
masthead.lede: A record of what was built and in what order, written as it went. The estimates are left in place beside the actuals, because a journal that quietly corrects them stops being useful for the next estimate.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.title: What exists now that did not before.

items.text: A vehicle inside a zone does not re-alert every tick; it alerts on the transition and again on exit, which is the whole reason step 3 took as long as it did.

items.lead: Zones are evaluated against the last known position, not a live stream.
items.text: A vehicle out of coverage for twenty minutes is not treated as having left its zone. It is treated as unknown, and unknown is not an alert.
The flag is off for every fleet. Turning it on is a separate decision with its own board.

sections.label: The overrun
sections.title: Why transition state cost four days instead of one.

blocks.text: The estimate assumed a vehicle is either inside a zone or outside it. Neither the GPS nor the network agrees: positions arrive late, out of order, and sometimes twice. The first implementation alerted on every reordered pair.

blocks.caption: What replaced the naive comparison

comments.text: Dropping an older fix silently is right for alerting and wrong for the position history, which is written by a different path. Worth stating in the function's own docs that this is not the historian.

blocks.title: The estimate was not wrong about the work
blocks.lead: It was wrong about the data.
blocks.text: Point-in-polygon really was half a day. What cost four was discovering that the position feed is unordered — which is written down nowhere, and which the next person to build against it will also discover this way unless this journal is read.

blocks.label: Feed ordering
blocks.ask: Where should the fact that the position feed is unordered be written down so the next build does not rediscover it?
blocks.placeholder: e.g. the feed's own README, the platform data catalogue, a doc comment on the client
